items.title: M1 freeze Authority vocabulary migration contract
items.context: Create a source-of-truth migration/retirement document that defines banned active vocabulary, replacement local assurance/admissibility terms, and explicit legacy whitelist rules. Verification must prove the contract exists and is referenced by the scanner.
items.userSees: User sees: `retired authority vocabulary contract: PASS (banned=5, replacements=6, whitelist=explicit)`.

happy.desc: Migration contract exists and defines banned active terms plus replacement local assurance/admissibility vocabulary.

edge.desc: Contract distinguishes active surfaces from explicit legacy whitelist so historical docs can exist without weakening the active scanner.

adversarial.desc: A scanner or smoke must reference the contract so the document is not prose-only and cannot be bypassed at DONE.

items.title: M2 clean user-facing Authority wording
items.context: Update README, guide/docs, agent prompts/templates, CLI help/catalog text, DONE/user-facing output language so active surfaces no longer say Authority Server or productionDone-style no-overclaim wording; use local assurance/admissibility/evidence scope terms instead.
items.userSees: User sees: `retired authority vocabulary scan: PASS active user-facing surfaces use local assurance terms`.

happy.desc: Active user-facing docs, prompts, and help output use local assurance/admissibility vocabulary.

edge.desc: Explicit retired legacy docs may keep historical terms only inside whitelist context and must not appear as active guidance.

adversarial.desc: Generated `lattice help` output is scanned so old wording cannot hide in command descriptions.

items.title: M3 remove Authority command surface from active CLI
items.context: Remove authority_* active commands from help/catalog/config and hide/delete legacy compatibility surfaces. Verification must inspect CLI help/catalog/config, not just source text.
items.userSees: User sees: `command surface scan: PASS active authority_* commands=0`.

happy.desc: CLI help/catalog/config expose local assurance commands but no active authority_* server-backed command surface.

edge.desc: Any compatibility alias is hidden legacy/quarantined and absent from normal help/catalog output.

adversarial.desc: A scanner positive-control catches active authority_* command exposure if reintroduced.

items.title: M4 remove or quarantine server-backed Authority code and smokes
items.context: Delete or isolate server-backed authority client/runner/receipt-gate modules and corresponding smoke tasks. Preserve local quorum_submit, proof-admissibility, receipt-bundle, delivery-check, and local lifecycle gates.
items.userSees: User sees: `authority quarantine scan: PASS server-backed runtime imports=0; local proof smokes=PASS`.

happy.desc: Server-backed Authority modules/smokes are absent from active runtime imports or explicitly quarantined, while local proof features still pass.

edge.desc: Shared helpers/types needed by local quorum/admissibility/receipt-bundle are preserved or renamed without breaking build.

adversarial.desc: Scanner fails if active runtime paths import quarantined server-backed Authority modules.

items.title: M5 add hard retired-Authority scanner gate
items.context: Add a hard scanner/smoke that fails if active core code or active docs contain Authority Server, authorityDone, fullAuthorityDone, productionDone, or LATTICE_AUTHORITY_* outside explicit legacy/migration whitelist. This scanner must be part of validation so DONE cannot pass with drift.
items.userSees: User sees the retired-Authority scanner pass in validation and fail closed for active banned vocabulary outside the legacy whitelist.

happy.desc: The retired-Authority scanner passes current active docs/code/help/catalog and is included in configured validation.

edge.desc: Legacy whitelist/migration docs are permitted only by explicit path/section rules and remain visible in scanner output.

adversarial.desc: Positive-control samples for Authority Server, authorityDone, fullAuthorityDone, productionDone, LATTICE_AUTHORITY_*, and active authority_* command exposure are rejected.
